postal_code.description: The postal code attached to the credit card.

credit_card.description: Your actual credit card THAT WILL GET CHARGED.

email_address.description: The email address to receive order updates and a receipt to.

block.description:
The Dominos provider is used to interact with resources supported by Dominos Pizza.
The provider needs to be configured with a credit card for ordering.

Use the navigation to the right to read about the available resources.

api_object.description: The computed json payload for the specified address.

item_codes.description: An array of menu items to order.

price_only.description: DRY RUN: This will only display the total price of the order (and not actually order).

store_id.description: The ID of the store that the order is for.

total_price.description: The computed total price of the order.

block.description:
This is it! This will order you your pizzas!

As far as I know there is no way to cancel a dominos order programmatically, so if you made a mistake, you'll have to call the store.
You should receive an email confirmation almost instantly, and that email will have the store's phone number in it.

api_object.description: The computed json payload for the specified address.

city.description: The city to deliver the pizza to. Ex: 'Anytown'.

postal_code.description: The region to deliver the pizza to (or zip for the USA). Ex: 'A1A1A1'.

region.description: The region to deliver the pizza to, meaning the province or state. Ex: 'BC'.

street.description: The street to deliver the pizza to. Ex: '123 Main St'.

type.description: The type of location to deliver to. Default: 'House'.

url_object.description: The computed line1 & line2 for the specified address.

block.description:
This data source takes in the delivery address and writes it back out in the two different JSON formats that the API expects.

For carryout, this is purely to find the closest store.

code.description: The dominos code for the item.

price_cents.description: The price in cents of the item.

menu.description: An array of all menu item for the given store.

store_id.description: The ID of the store to get the menu for.

block.description:
If you would prefer to do your own filtering, you can get access to every item on the dominos menu in your area using this data source.
This data source takes in store_id and provides menu, a list of all (186, at my dominos) name/code/price_cents blocks.

For the love of all that's holy, do not accidentally feed this data source directly into the dominos_order.
This will be expensive and probably pretty annoying to the Dominos store, which will be serving you 1 of each 2-liter bottle of soda, 1 of each 20oz bottle, at least 4 different kinds of salad, probably like 6 different kinds of chicken wings, and I think 12 of each kind of pizza?
(Small, medium, large) x (Hand Tossed, Pan, Stuffed Crust, Gluten Free)?
Oh plus breads. There's breads on the menu, I found that out while trawling through API responses.
I wonder who eats those. Are they good? Let me know!

code.description: The dominos code for the item.

price_cents.description: The price in cents of the item.

matches.description: An array of all possible menu item that matches the given query string.

query_string.description: Each string in query_string must literally match the name of the menu item for the menu item to appear in matches.

store_id.description: The ID of the store to get the menu for.

block.description:
This data source takes in the store_id and a list of strings (as query_string), and outputs the menu items in matches.
Each item in matches has three attributes: name, code, and price_cents.
The name is human-readable, but not useful for ordering.
The price_cents is also only informational.

Each string in query_string must literally match the name of the menu item for the menu item to appear in matches.

address_url_object.description: The required line1 & line2 for the specified address.

delivery_minutes.description: The estimated minutes until your pizza will be delivered.

store_id.description: The ID of the store closest to the address.

block.description: Provided a Dominos address, this data source returns the store_id of the closest Dominos store, and, in case it's useful to you somehow, the delivery_minutes, an integer showing the estimated minutes until your pizza will be delivered.
